fxRates.description: Source-linked FX observations. A rate is used only for its exact applicable period and declared conversion direction.

precedenceRules.description: Reviewed, scope-exact decisions that select one observation and enumerate every superseded competing identity.

meaning.description: A meaning-preservation problem you have already found, from an assessment such as POST /api/v2/context/assess-meaning. Only the cautious states are accepted: "changed" and "ambiguous" stop a citation presenting as verified. "faithful" is deliberately NOT accepted here — a clearance asserted by the party asking for the check is not a check, and this field exists precisely so that "nobody assessed this" cannot be mistaken for "an assessor cleared this". Omit it when you found no problem; the result then reports meaning "not_checked", which is what absence honestly means.

quote.description: The claim or quote to check.

source_text.description: The source text to check the quote against. Provide this, or url, or asset_id.

grounded.description: True when the quote was found in the resolved source.

code.description:
The stable classification of `reason`, safe to switch on. The same vocabulary and the same values as `POST /extract`. Null when nothing refused.

| Code | What it means | What to do |
|------|---------------|------------|
| `source_too_large` | a size or expansion ceiling refused the read | `reason` carries the observed value and the limit; send a smaller file |
| `source_encrypted` | the container is password-protected | send an unlocked copy |
| `source_corrupt` | the container could not be opened as the format it declares | re-export the file |
| `unsupported_format` | no reader is registered for this format | convert it |
| `ocr_unavailable` | the page had no text layer and no vision provider is configured | configure a vision key, or send a text-layer file |
| `partial_extraction` | some of the source was recovered and some was not | use what came back |
| `empty_source` | the source was read and held nothing | a fact about the file, not a failure — nothing to retry |
| `extraction_error` | our failure | retry |

Carries detail no enum can, and is NOT stable: it includes dependency error text. Display it; do not branch on it. Null when nothing refused.

mode.description: How PDF pages and images are read on `/extract` and `/extract/pages`. `lite` is the faster, lower-cost read, about 0.12 credits a page. `standard` is the higher-accuracy read for each page type, about 0.75 credits a page, with a second read for form pages and for a read that fails; it does better on complex tables, handwriting and scans. Every other step is the same in both modes: the reading is checked against the page's text layer and drawing, long tables are read again in row bands, chart values are measured from the drawing, and form and table rules apply. A lite read and a standard read of the same file are kept apart; neither is served for the other. Spreadsheets and text documents are read the same way in both modes. With no mode, an account created on or after 20 November 2026 (04:00 UTC) reads in lite; an account created before then keeps standard, as before, and can send `lite` to opt in. A visual rendition is read in standard mode.

refresh.description: Read the file again even when the same content was read before in this account, and keep the new complete read in place of the earlier one. The new read is charged. Default false.

source_version_id.description: Exact immutable owned source version for visual_rendition.

visual_rendition.description: Explicit JPEG/PNG visual layout rendition. Requires owned asset_id, exact source_version_id and Idempotency-Key. Source remains partial; does not select the rendition.

code.description:
The stable classification of `reason`, safe to switch on. Null on a complete read.

| Code | What it means | What to do |
|------|---------------|------------|
| `source_too_large` | a size or expansion ceiling refused the read | `reason` carries the observed value and the limit; send a smaller file |
| `source_encrypted` | the container is password-protected | send an unlocked copy |
| `source_corrupt` | the container could not be opened as the format it declares | re-export the file |
| `unsupported_format` | no reader is registered for this format | convert it |
| `ocr_unavailable` | the page had no text layer and no vision provider is configured | configure a vision key, or send a text-layer file |
| `partial_extraction` | some of the source was recovered and some was not | use what came back; `lost[]` names the rest |
| `empty_source` | the source was read and held nothing | a fact about the file, not a failure — nothing to retry |
| `extraction_error` | our failure | retry |

complete.description: Present, and only ever `false`, when the read did not recover the whole source. Absent on a complete read, so seeing it is a determination rather than a default.

credit_usage.description: The charge with a snapshot of the account balance. The same figures are sent as `X-Credits-*` response headers.

extraction_method.description: The path that produced most of this document's text.

format.description: The format the bytes were read as.

lost.description: The parts that were not recovered. Absent on a complete read.

markdown.description: The whole document as markdown. Empty when nothing was read.

operation_id.description: Identifier of this billed operation. Quote it when asking about a charge.

reason.description: Free text naming the cause, straight from whatever refused or failed — `extraction_failed:File is password-protected`, `spreadsheet_too_large:bytes:33554433>33554432`. Carries detail no enum can (the observed value and the limit are both in it) and is NOT stable: it includes dependency error text. Display it; do not branch on it. Null on a complete read.

sheets.description: Spreadsheets only: every sheet the workbook declares, in workbook order, with its structure and read state.

state.description: How much of the source the read recovered, in one word.

units.description: The document part by part, in source order: one unit per page or sheet. Empty when nothing was read.

usage.description: What this request was charged: the metered cost of its page reads, in credits to 4 decimal places. 0 when nothing readable came back or no page image was read.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the unit content, when the reader recorded one.

elements.description: The page as typed blocks in reading order, each with a box. Present on visually read pages, and on a text-layer page whose blocks could be placed from the text layer; absent otherwise.

extraction_method.description: How this unit's text was produced. `ocr` means the page image was read.

geometry.description: Present with `elements`: the page size and the coordinate system of the boxes.

image_input.description: Present when a page with a text layer was read from its rendered image instead of the PDF, because the text layer does not carry the printed text: the checks that found it. `unmapped`: the layer holds control or private-use characters where the page prints letters. `garbled`: the layer's words have the shapes of a broken font map. `hidden` (lite mode only): the layer is drawn invisibly under a scan, an embedded OCR layer.

index.description: 1-based position of the part in the document.

kind.description: The kind of part: `page` for PDFs and images, `sheet` for spreadsheets; other formats name their own parts (`slide`, `document`, `table`, `message_body`, ...).

mode.description: Present on every unit of a `mode: "lite"` request; absent on a standard request.

provenance.description: Where in the source this unit came from.

reader.description: Visually read pages only, when the server routes pages by type: the kind of page it was read as.

reason.description: Present with `state`: free text naming what went wrong on this unit. Display it; do not branch on it.

sheet.description: Sheet units only: the tab's native structure (`name`, `visibility`, `merges`, and `cells` when the workbook was parsed for this request).

state.description: Present only when this unit was not read completely. The same unit is named in `lost[]`.

text.description: The part as Markdown (CSV for a sheet). On a page with `elements` it is the same reading as the elements in order.

credits.description: Credits actually deducted; null when a priced operation was not metered. Zero denotes a genuinely free operation.

page_charges.description: One line for each page charged. The lines add up to `credits` to within rounding; when the charge stopped at the balance, `credits` is lower than their sum.

pages.description: Pages this request was charged for: the PDF pages and images that came back with text. A page that could not be read is not counted. 0 for a spreadsheet or a text document, which no model reads.

basis.description: Whether the figure is actual, forecast, assumed or unknown.

currency.description: Currency code of the normalized value.

decimalValue.description: Canonical decimal text used for exact arithmetic. Without it the figure can be reported but not recomputed.

observationId.description: Immutable observation identity. Exact replay may reuse it.

scale.description: Scale qualifier for the already-normalized value. This does not apply another conversion.

value.description: Value normalized to the metric canonical unit.

decimalRate.description: Canonical decimal rate used by exact arithmetic.

category.description: The category whose expected-documents checklist to compute.

docs.description: The documents currently filed in that category.

stage.description: Stage to tailor the checklist to.

evidence_role.description: Whether cited sources take a position on this claim or provide context only; absent means unassessed.

finding.example: The event occurred on the stated date according to official records

code.description: The stable classification of this part's `reason`. Same vocabulary as the document-level `code`; the two can differ, because a document that recovered most of itself is `partial_extraction` while the one part it lost names its own cause.

index.description: 1-based page / sheet index, as on the unit that failed.

kind.description: Which kind of unit was lost.

reason.description: Free text: what the reader said about this part.

sheet.description: Sheet units only: the tab the workbook declared.

state.description: What happened to this part specifically.

hasNextPage.description: Whether there is a next page

hasPreviousPage.description: Whether there is a previous page

recency.description: Publication freshness score (0-100). Current year = 100, decreases with age.

source_authority.description: Domain reputation score (0-100). Higher scores for government, academic, major news sources.

analysis_model.description: Identifier of the analysis configuration that produced the result

constraint.description: Explicit constraint accounting: searched vs kept, plus dropped host classes (not publisher names).

relevant_sources_found.description: Number of relevant sources found and included

source_url_reads.description: Per supplied-URL read receipts, with fetched_at from retained capture time or null when unknown. Present for authenticated DD/eval; omitted on public MCP.

answer.description: POST /citation/chat only. The typed answer: sections of claims, each citing one or more returned citation ids (one id per entry, never a range), and unknown blocks for parts of the question the sources do not answer. When present, search_result_with_citations_mapping is rendered from it. Null unless answer_status is valid.

answer_status.description: POST /citation/chat only. valid: answer validated (after at most one model retry). invalid: it failed validation twice. model_error: the model call failed. no_answer_text: there was no grounded answer to type (for example a cached replay). In every case but valid, search_result_with_citations_mapping is the original grounded text.

The engine's measured accuracy against a gold-set corpus: conflict detection recall and precision, and recompute correctness. Reproducible and gated on every build — an accuracy regression cannot ship.

post.description:
Document-in numeric analysis. Give an uploaded asset id; the document is downloaded, its figures are extracted, then recomputed and cross-checked. Returns the extracted figures alongside conflicts, recomputations, and a review flag.

- **Spreadsheets** (xlsx/xls/csv): extracted deterministically with exact cell provenance. A cell read is exact, so these are rule reads. Server compute and file I/O only.
- **PDFs**: the printed figures are read from the page image (never computed); these are model reads, capped at needs_review and never presented as verified. Their value is cross-source, e.g. a deck figure that disagrees with the spreadsheet. **This path makes a paid read of each page image.**

**Cost: 3 credits.** The document is downloaded and parsed; PDF pages may also be read from their images. Rate-limited more strictly than compute-only endpoints.

post.description:
Resolve a citation back to its exact source and render it, so you can show the evidence behind a claim.

- **Web sources** (`url`): returns a text-fragment deep link (`url#:~:text=quote`) that scrolls a browser to the quote.
- **Document sources** (`asset_id`, from POST /upload): returns the cited page's extracted text and a `asset_url#page=N` deep link. Spreadsheets return the sheet grid.

Every preview includes a **bindBack** result: whether the cited quote is actually present in the source (`grounded`) and how it matched (`exact`, `normalized`, `fuzzy`, `reflowed`, or `unbound`). A `reflowed` match used a derived OCR reading and always requires review. A citation that cannot be bound back is never reported as grounded.

**Cost: 1 credit.** Deterministic, but a web preview fetches the source URL, so this endpoint is subject to your plan's rate limits.

post.description:
Deterministic, model-free document classification. Downloads an uploaded asset, extracts its content + spreadsheet sheet names, and returns a coarse **category** plus the fine multi-type **covers** it holds (a bundled workbook covers several). Works with no model configured (air-gapped safe).

Pass an optional `taxonomy` preset (`vc` = venture data-room, `ma` = M&A categories; default `vc`).

**`unfiled` is an answer, not a failure.** A document that was read completely and matched no category gets it, so it cannot also mean "we never read this". `state`, `reason` and `code` — the same three fields, the same vocabulary and the same values as `POST /extract` — say whether the classifier ever saw any content. A refused, corrupt, unsupported or unreadable asset returns `unfiled` with a non-null `code`; a genuinely empty document returns `unfiled` with `code: "empty_source"`; a complete read returns `code: null`. `category` and `covers` are untouched by this — anything routing on them today keeps working.

**Cost: 1 credit.** Deterministic, but downloads + parses the asset.
post.summary: Classify a document into a category and covered types

post.description:
All-formats extraction (PDF, JPEG/PNG images, spreadsheets, docx/pptx/html/txt, …) into a normalized document: whole-doc `markdown`, per-page/sheet `units` with page/sheet provenance, and (for spreadsheets) sheet names. Extraction never hard-fails: an unreadable asset returns empty text. The request is synchronous: the response is the finished document, and there is no job to poll.

**How pages are read.** Spreadsheets and text formats are read deterministically from the file. Every PDF page, and a JPEG or PNG as a one-page document, is read from its rendered image, and the reading is checked against the page's own text layer and drawing where the page has them. Before the read, each page is given a page type (`scan`, `form`, `dense`, `table`, `chart`, `complex_text`, `plain_text`). In lite mode every page gets the faster, lower-cost read; in standard mode each page gets the higher-accuracy read for its page type, and a second read takes over when the first fails. Such a unit has `extraction_method: "ocr"`, a `reader` naming the page type, `elements` (typed blocks in reading order, each with its Markdown and a normalized `bbox`) and the page `geometry`. A page whose read could not be completed falls back to its text layer (or, in standard mode, plain OCR): it has no `reader`, may have no `elements`, and is reported through `state` and `lost[]`.

**Lite and standard.** `mode: "lite"` is the faster, lower-cost read, about 0.12 credits a page. `mode: "standard"` is the higher-accuracy read, about 0.75 credits a page, which does better on complex tables, handwriting and scans. A request with no `mode` reads in lite for an account created on or after 20 November 2026 (04:00 UTC); an account created before then keeps standard as its default, with the same price, estimate and response as before, and can send `mode: "lite"` to opt in. Either mode can always be sent explicitly. Every other step is the same in both modes: the reading is checked against the page's text layer and drawing, long tables are read again in row bands, chart values are measured from the drawing, and the form and table rules apply. Lite also reads a page whose text is a hidden OCR layer (an invisible text layer under a scan, with no other text printed over it) from its rendered image, and `image_input` then names `hidden`. In lite a form page is not read a second time, and a page whose read fails after its retry is not read another way: it keeps its text layer or is reported through `state` and `lost[]`, and is not charged. Each unit of a lite read carries `mode: "lite"`; a standard read carries no `mode`. A lite read and a standard read of the same file are kept apart: neither is served for the other. A visual rendition is read in standard mode.

**A partial read says so.** When the file opened but a part of it could not be read (a workbook sheet whose part the package is missing, a page that failed), the response carries `complete: false` and `lost[]` naming what was not recovered (sheet or page, and why). Both keys are absent from a complete read, so seeing either is a finding rather than a default, and `state` (`complete` | `partial` | `error` | `unsupported`) is the same determination in one word. `unsupported` was served but not listed here: it is the answer for a format no reader is registered for, and a consumer switching on the documented three fell through on it.

**Why a read did not complete, in two fields.** `reason` is free text straight from whatever refused or failed, so it carries detail no enum can: `spreadsheet_too_large:bytes:33554433>33554432` has the observed value and the limit in it. It is not stable: it includes dependency error text such as `extraction_failed:Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Pages')`. Failure text from the service that read a page (its name, a model id, an endpoint or its own error wording) is never passed on: in `reason`, `error` and `message` it is replaced with `the document could not be read` for the document, or `the page could not be read` inside a unit or a `lost[]` entry, and the code before the colon is kept, as in `extraction_failed:the document could not be read`. `code` is the stable classification of the same refusal, and it is the one to switch on.

| `code` | Meaning | Caller's move |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `source_too_large` | a size or expansion ceiling refused the read | send a smaller file; `reason` has the numbers |
| `source_encrypted` | the container is password-protected | send an unlocked copy |
| `source_corrupt` | the container could not be opened as the format it declares | re-export the file |
| `unsupported_format` | no reader is registered for this format | convert it |
| `ocr_unavailable` | no text layer, and page-image reading is not configured | send a text-layer file |
| `partial_extraction` | some of the source came back and some did not | use what came back; `lost[]` names the rest |
| `empty_source` | the source was read and held nothing | nothing to retry: this is a fact about the file |
| `extraction_error` | our failure | retry |

Both are `null` on a complete read. Each `lost[]` entry carries its own `reason` and `code` for the part it names, which can differ from the document's: a workbook that lost one sheet of two is `partial_extraction` while the lost sheet is `source_corrupt`.

**`extraction_method`** says which path produced the text, so a consumer storing this as evidence can tell a deterministic read from a model transcription:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `text_layer` | the file's own machine-readable text, read deterministically |
| `ocr` | no text layer, so the page image was transcribed |
| `spreadsheet_cells` | cells read out of the workbook, no model and no rendering |
| `none` | nothing readable came back (empty, unparseable, or a scan with no OCR configured) |

A document can mix paths, such as a text-layer PDF with two scanned pages in it. The top-level `extraction_method` is then the **dominant** path (the one behind the most readable units, ties going to `ocr`); `units[].extraction_method` is the exact answer for that page or sheet.

**Spreadsheet units** also carry `sheet`: the tab's native structure straight from the workbook. `sheet.merges` lists the merged ranges (`["A1:A2","B1:C1"]`) and `sheet.cells[].merged_range` says which range each cell belongs to, so a header spanning two columns can be rebuilt: the `text` CSV flattens it to a value plus a blank.

**Cost: metered, at cost.** Each page is charged what its read costs at list prices, converted at $0.04 a credit, as a decimal number of credits (4 decimal places). A lite page costs about 0.12 credits (0 cents) and a standard page about 0.75 credits (3 cents); a page of plain text costs less and a dense table more. One page is never charged more than 10 credits ($0.40). A page that could not be read is free, and so is a spreadsheet or a text document (docx, pptx, html, txt), which is read from the file directly.

**Reading the receipt.** `usage.credits` is the amount deducted, `usage.pages` the number of pages charged, and `usage.page_charges` one line a page with its `page_type` and `credits`. The lines add up to `usage.credits` to within rounding.

**Before the read.** The cost is known only after the pages are read, so a PDF is first checked against an estimate: its page count at 0.12 credits a page for a lite read or 0.75 for a standard read. When the balance is under the estimate and the account has no overage billing, the request is refused with `400` naming the credits required and available, nothing is read and nothing is charged. A document is read whole or not at all. If the pages cost more than the balance holds, the charge stops at the balance, which never goes below zero; accounts with overage billing are charged the full cost.

**Repeated files.** A PDF or image whose exact content this account had read completely in the last 24 hours, under the same reader build, is answered from that read: no page is read again and nothing is charged (`usage.credits` 0). Send `refresh: true` to read it again anyway (for example to compare two reads); the new read is charged and, when complete, replaces the earlier one.

**Limits.** The asset can be at most 100 MB (`413` above that), and its download into the reader has 30 seconds (`504`). This endpoint is rate limited at half the plan's request limits (per minute and per day); a `429` carries a `Retry-After` header and `retryAfter` seconds in the body. A long document is read page by page inside the one request, so allow a client timeout of several minutes.

201.description: The extracted document: { format, markdown, extraction_method, state, reason, code, units[], sheets?[], complete?: false, lost?[], operation_id, usage, credit_usage }

400.description: asset_url is not an allowed public web address, neither asset_id nor asset_url was given, `mode` is not `standard` or `lite`, `mode: "lite"` was sent with a visual rendition, or the balance is under the estimate for the document, its page count at 0.12 credits a page in lite or 0.75 in standard (`Insufficient credits. Required: 0.75, Available: 0. …` for a one-page PDF read in standard). The body has `message`, `error`, `statusCode` and `credit_usage`

404.description: The asset does not exist, or the store has no bytes for it

413.description: The asset is over the 100 MB download ceiling. The body carries `bytes` (null when the reader refused mid-stream) and `max_bytes`

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. `Retry-After` header and body `{ statusCode, message, error, retryAfter, limit, remaining, plan }`, `retryAfter` in seconds

502.description: The asset store returned a failure. Ours, not the request: retry

503.description: Private evidence storage is not configured, so an evidence:// asset cannot be read

504.description: The asset download timed out. Retry

post.description:
Reads a spreadsheet and returns each known metric as a **figure**: the value normalized to its canonical unit, plus what it means (`metric`), `unit`, optional `entity`/`period`, a confidence `band`, whether it was confirmed against the cited cell (`bound`), and full `provenance` (asset, sheet, cell, source label). This is deterministic financial-model reading: header scale ("$M"/"'000"), accounting negatives, period columns (FY2023 vs FY2024), and unit-declaration checks are all honoured, so a % is never mis-read as currency.

Deterministic-first. Reads **spreadsheets** (cell-level discovery), **PDFs with a text layer** (grounded and cited by page), and **every other text-bearing format** (docx, pptx, html, txt) deterministically with no model calls. **Scanned PDF pages and image files** (png/jpg/...) are transcribed by vision OCR first, then grounded, so their numbers are still extracted (provenance marked `model`); this needs page-image reading on the server and is skipped otherwise. Accepts `asset_id` (uploaded asset) or `asset_url` (your own signed URL).

**An empty `figures` says why it is empty.** `state`, `reason` and `code` — the same three fields, the same vocabulary and the same values as `POST /extract` — describe **the read that fed the figure engine**, not the figure list. A workbook that opened and yielded no known metric is `state: "complete"` with `code: null`: the engine measured it and found nothing to tag, which is an answer. A refusal never reached the engine and carries its cause (`source_too_large`, `source_corrupt`, `source_encrypted`, `unsupported_format`, `extraction_error`). `figures` itself is untouched.

**Cost: 2 credits.** Deterministic; downloads and runs the full figure engine over every sheet/page.

200.description: { figures: { metric, value, unit, entity?, period?, band, bound, provenance }[], state, reason, code }

post.summary: Extract every number from a document as a tagged, source-grounded figure

post.description:
The same all-formats extraction as POST /extract, sliced into retrieval-sized **chunks** that keep the anchor a citation needs: `page` (PDF), `sheet` (workbook tab), `section` (nearest preceding markdown heading), plus a `token_estimate` for packing a context budget. `ordinal` is contiguous from 0 across the whole document.

Use this instead of /extract when you intend to index the text and later point a reader at where a passage came from: flat pages cannot carry a citation.

**An empty `chunks` says why it is empty.** `state`, `reason` and `code` are the extraction's own determination, carried through verbatim: the same three fields, the same vocabulary and the same values as `POST /extract` over the same asset. A refusal (`source_too_large`, `source_corrupt`, `source_encrypted`, `unsupported_format`) and a document that genuinely holds nothing (`empty_source`) both return no chunks, and `code` is what tells them apart. `code` is `null` on a complete read.

**Cost: metered, at cost.** Each page is charged what its read costs at list prices, converted at $0.04 a credit, as a decimal number of credits (4 decimal places). A lite page costs about 0.12 credits (0 cents) and a standard page about 0.75 credits (3 cents); a page of plain text costs less and a dense table more. One page is never charged more than 10 credits ($0.40). A page that could not be read is free, and so is a spreadsheet or a text document (docx, pptx, html, txt), which is read from the file directly. The same price as /extract: the chunking is in-process and makes no model call. A repeated file is answered from the earlier read as on /extract, and `refresh: true` reads it again.

**Lite and standard.** As on /extract: `mode: "lite"` is the faster, lower-cost read and `mode: "standard"` the higher-accuracy read; with no `mode`, an account created on or after 20 November 2026 (04:00 UTC) reads in lite and an older account keeps standard. The response carries `mode: "lite"` for a lite read.

400.description: Asset not found, `mode` is not `standard` or `lite`, or the balance is under the estimate for the document (the same `Insufficient credits.` refusal as POST /extract)

post.summary: Extract a document into anchored chunks ready to index and cite

post.description:
Given the documents already filed in a category, returns each expected document type flagged present/absent. An item is present when any document matches it by filename, category, or covered type. Advisory — nothing blocks the workflow. Pure and deterministic; no I/O.

Pass an optional `taxonomy` preset and `stage` (`early`/`growth`) to tailor the list.

**Cost: 1 credit.** Pure and deterministic (no I/O).

post.description:
Search for authoritative sources related to a query. Returns raw citations without stance analysis or verdict.

**Credits: 2** (search only)

Store a file and get the `asset_id` that `POST /extract` and the other document endpoints take. Send `multipart/form-data` with one `file` part; the part's filename decides the format, so keep its extension.

**Cost: 0 credits.** Uploading is free and needs no credit balance; `usage.credits` is 0. Reading the file with `POST /extract` is charged for each page read.

**Limits.** The file can be at most 100 MB and must not be empty. Uploads are not counted against the plan's request limits; the general limit of 300 requests per minute applies and answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Verify a factual claim against authoritative sources. Returns sources with stance analysis and an overall verdict. When a wrong clause has a proven replacement, verdict.corrections contains a corrected_statement and exact proof quotes tied to citations in the same claim group. correction_status is not_established when the evidence cannot prove a replacement.

**Credit System:**
| Operation | Credits | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Search | 2 | Find sources for the claim |
| Stance Analysis | 1 | Analyze stance of each source (set include_stance=false to skip) |
| Verdict | 1 | Generate overall verdict (set include_verdict=false to skip) |

The fixed prices are:

| include_stance | include_verdict | Credits |
|----------------|-----------------|---------|
| false | false | 2 |
| true | false | 3 |
| false | true | 4 |
| true | true | 4 |

Verdict generation requires stance analysis internally, so verdict-only costs 4. Cached and uncached V1 requests use the same price.

App keys require evidence_scope with a readable folder and verify permission. This scoped route retrieves filed-source citations at zero credits, returns support:not_checked and verdict:null, and does not run public-web verification.

Reuse with the same request to recover a completed result without regenerating or charging twice. Different payload returns 409. Completed checkpoints are retained for 24 hours; missing checkpoints or unresolved accounting return 503 instead of repeating work. This header contract applies to JSON verify only.

post.description:
Bind every claim to its source in a single request. Each item is a quote plus its source (inline text, a url, or an asset). The response gives, per item, whether the quote is grounded, how it matched (exact, normalized, fuzzy, reflowed, or unbound), the best-matching passage and score even when unbound, the verification tier, and a feedback token.

A fuzzy match is capped at needs_review, never verified. A reflowed match uses a derived OCR reading and is also capped at needs_review. Use this to check every citation in a document at once.

App keys require evidence_scope with a readable folder and verify permission. Their items must omit source_text, url, asset_id, source_version_id, representation_id and source_unit_id. Each quote is grounded in filed-source citations; unmatched quotes return explicit item errors. The folder organization billing owner pays the batch, after scope and payer validation.

**Cost: 1 credit per item.** BindBack is deterministic, but a batch can be large and `url`/`asset` items fetch their source, so this endpoint is rate-limited more strictly than compute-only endpoints.

Reuse with the same body (the whole validated request) to recover a completed result without re-running or charging twice. A different body or changed app-batch billing owner returns 409; a repeat while the first is running returns 503. Completed results are retained for 24 hours.

Stream verification results via Server-Sent Events. Citations stream as processed, followed by verdict when requested.

certificate.description: Rerunnable receipt in the ProofArtifact shape. status is proved (supported), refuted (contradicted), unknown (escalate) or not_applicable. An independent checker recomputes the verdict from witness alone; check reports agreement or each disagreement. Figure readings, printed facet values and semantic comparability facets are premises bound by bindingHash and proofHash, not recomputed. Not persisted.

post.description:
Fetches the file server-side and stores it exactly like a multipart upload, returning asset_id and source_version_id for review and extraction.

The URL must be public HTTPS. Every redirect hop is re-checked; private, loopback, link-local, metadata, multicast and reserved addresses (IPv4 and IPv6) are refused, no caller credentials or headers are forwarded, the body is capped at 100 MB while streaming and the fetch times out after 30 s. The bytes must be one of: PDF, PNG, JPEG, WebP, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, XLSM, XLSB, XLS, ODS, CSV, TSV, TXT, MD.

**Cost: 0 credits.** Uploading is free and needs no credit balance; `usage.credits` is 0.
